line: An answer as a QR code on screen, to carry it to your phone without the network.

name: quake-bets
line: Will there be a magnitude 6 this week? Bet, then let the USGS feed settle it against the base rate.
network: earthquake.usgs.gov, to read the week's earthquakes

name: quantized
line: Finds the smallest quantized local model that still gets your box's own questions right, so suggestions come faster.
needs: a local model server; licence varies by model

name: quiet-corner
line: A Quiet Corner backup file: a teacher's classroom observations as dated passages, for that teacher's questions alone.

name: quiz
line: A quiz from your own files: a passage with a word missing, and you fill it in.

name: quote-review
line: A review comment that quotes the repo, checked: does the quoted line still say that at the pull request's head?
network: the forge, through the workflow's token, to read the review comments

name: reading-level
line: How hard a passage reads (sentence length, word length, Flesch), so a teacher can find texts for a class.

name: reading-log
line: A child's reading log: books, pages and minutes, week by week.

name: readwise
line: Readwise's highlights export: every highlight with its book or article, and your note on it.

name: real-sky
line: A horoscope from where the planets really are, computed offline from a JPL ephemeris.

name: recipes
line: Recipes from saved web pages and recipe-app exports, as plain text: what can I cook with leeks?

name: reconciler
line: willow-reconciler run on this repo's idea list and git history: how much of what was proposed has landed.

name: record-sql
line: SQL straight over your record, in place: 'how many answers did I approve in March?'

name: reddit
line: Reddit's data export: your posts, comments and saved items as dated lines.

name: redential
line: The bundle redential-cli's scan makes, written to the record before you submit it, so what left your machine can be checked later.
needs: the redential program, run through npx; Apache-2.0

name: renewals
line: Passports, licences, insurance and memberships: when each expires, from your documents.

name: report
line: A self-checking bundle: the record, the approved answers, and a script that re-verifies them on any machine.

name: repro
line: A release built twice from the same commit, byte for byte the same.

name: rerank
line: A small model on the CPU that reorders the top passages by reading the question and each passage together.

name: retire
line: Proposes setting aside approved answers that no longer hold, each one gone only when you seal it.

name: reversi
line: Reversi as rows: every move, each flip following from the board.

name: ripgrep
line: Exact search through ripgrep, much faster on a big folder, its hits checked against the kernel's hashes.
needs: the ripgrep program; MIT or Unlicense

name: ro-crate
line: A box snapshot as an RO-Crate research object Zenodo can read: each file with its hash and licence.

name: roll-for-merge
line: A d20 for every pull request, green runs added and red streaks taken away, against a DC the bot calls.

name: rss-out
line: New approved answers as an RSS feed file, for any feed reader.

name: rtf
line: RTF documents as plain text.

name: rubric
line: Marking against a rubric you wrote: each mark cites the criterion and the line of work it's for.

name: rules
line: A game's or a house's rules, sealed section by section, so 'what does the rule say?' answers with the exact section.

name: safe-app
line: willow as a SAFE app: installed from the SAFE App Store, authorized per session, and deleted clean.

name: said
line: Your own quotes, gathered: every 'so-and-so, on this date: "..."' in your files, as a dated timeline of what was decided.

name: sap-gate
line: The mcp add-on's tool calls checked against SAP/1.0 grants before they run, through openclaw-sap-gate.

name: sarif
line: SARIF reports from code scanners such as CodeQL and Semgrep: each finding as a passage with its rule, file and line.

name: sbom
line: SBOMs in SPDX or CycloneDX JSON: each component, its version and licence, as passages.

name: school
line: School letters and emails for parents: trips, forms due, term dates, and what to bring.

name: scope
line: Hands an assistant only the passages in scope, as one file, by ids it can't guess: nothing outside it is named or counted.

name: screenplay
line: Fountain and Final Draft scripts: scenes, characters and lines, cited by scene.

name: scripture
line: A scripture or other canonical text with your study notes beside it, cited by book, chapter and verse.

name: scrivener
line: Scrivener projects: each document in the binder as plain text, by its place in the manuscript.

name: scrub
line: Strips the hidden details (EXIF, author, edit history) from a file before you share it.

name: second-opinion
line: Two assistants' suggestions for the same question side by side, each waiting for its own seal.

name: session-cost
line: Tokens each agent session spent, by day and by repo, summed from its own session files and priced from a table you keep.

name: session-seal
line: One seal at the end of a session, over everything asked and approved in it: yes, these were my actions.

name: share
line: One sealed answer to send someone, checkable by them, without giving them the folder.

name: sheets
line: Spreadsheets with formulas and formatting kept, beyond what the office add-on reads.

name: shell-history
line: Your bash, zsh and fish history: what you ran, and when the shell recorded it.

name: sigmap
line: SigMap's signature map of a codebase as plain text: each function's signature with its file and line, for questions about the code.

name: signal
line: A Signal backup, decrypted with its passphrase, as one dated line per message.

name: signed-commits
line: Which commits are signed, and by whose key, checked on this machine against the keys you trust.
needs: the git program; GPL, called not linked

name: slack
line: Slack's export zip: one dated line per message, with channel and author.

name: slow-tests
line: Each test's time kept per run, with the slowest named and any that got slower flagged.

name: snapshot
line: A web page or data file fetched once into the box, kept under its hash with its licence, so later answers cite the copy.
network: the address you give, fetched once

name: socratic
line: Asks you questions about your own notes instead of answering, each citing the passage it asked from.

name: sokoban
line: Sokoban levels and moves on the record, a solution checked by replaying it.

name: sourcehut
line: What willow's repo needs from SourceHut: its host.json for patches by email and a builds.sr.ht manifest.
network: sr.ht, through hut, to read the author of a patch a security report points to

name: speak
line: Reads answers aloud.

name: spurious
line: Everything joined on time and place (CI reds, earthquakes, rain, front pages) to hunt correlations that mean nothing.

name: standards
line: Curriculum standards beside your lessons: which standard each lesson meets, each cited.

name: static-search
line: An exported page of approved answers with its own search built in, no server, opened in any browser.

name: steam
line: Your Steam library from its local files: games, playtime and when you last played.

name: stems
line: Word forms for 20+ languages, so "maisons" finds "maison".

name: strava
line: Strava's export and GPX files: each run, ride and walk as a dated line with its distance and time.

name: student-records
line: A box of student records that answers only the teacher who owns it, and logs every look.

name: subscriptions
line: What you pay for every month, found in bank statements and emails, and when each renews.

name: subtitles
line: Subtitle and transcript files (.vtt, .srt) as lines cited by timestamp, for podcasts and videos already transcribed.

name: support-plan
line: An IEP or support plan's goals, accommodations and review dates, each cited, for a parent or teacher.

name: swift
line: A Swift port of kernel.py for iPhone and Mac apps, held to the same vectors.

name: syllabus
line: A course syllabus as dates: readings, assignments and exams due, each cited.

name: symbols
line: Exact definitions and references for Python code: where a name is defined, and every place it's used.

name: symptoms
line: A symptom diary over time, ready to show a doctor: what, when, how bad, each line cited.

name: sync
line: Your record kept on two devices through any synced folder, with the chain checked on each before it's trusted.

name: synonyms
line: Suggests words-list lines for a word no file has.

name: takeout
line: Google Takeout's My Activity and YouTube history, JSON or HTML, as dated lines.

name: tarot
line: A seeded tarot draw on the record, replayable by anyone with the seed.

name: tatoeba
line: A question in one language finds the same idea in another, through Tatoeba's sentence pairs, downloaded once.

name: tax-year
line: One tax year's receipts and statements gathered in one place, each with the file it came from.

name: teams
line: Microsoft Teams chats from your Microsoft account's export, one dated line per message.

name: telegram-bot
line: Ask from your phone through a Telegram bot only you can talk to.
network: api.telegram.org, to receive your questions and send answers

name: test-impact
line: Only the tests a change can reach run first, from the import graph; the full suite still runs after.

name: test-shards
line: The CI test jobs split by each test's past time, so every job finishes about together.

name: texts
line: Phone text messages, from an Android SMS backup or an iPhone backup's copy, one dated line per message.

name: thesis
line: A thesis's claims, each tied to the source that backs it, and a list of the ones with none.

name: tic-tac-toe
line: Tic-tac-toe as rows: every move, and the solver's value of each position; perfect play draws.

name: tides
line: Tide predictions as a control: if your Brier score on tides isn't near zero, the forecasting plumbing is broken.
network: NOAA's tides API, to read predictions and what happened

name: time-capsule
line: A note sealed now and opened on a date you choose, with the record proving it wasn't changed.

name: timeline
line: A dated timeline of one matter (a dispute, an illness, a tenancy), every line cited, to hand to a lawyer, doctor or council.

name: todays-place
line: One place a day drawn from Natural Earth's public-domain list, for the day's questions and bets.

name: transcript-redact
line: An agent transcript with keys, home paths and emails taken out before you share it, each removal listed by line.

name: translate
line: An answer translated by a local model, the original kept beside it, the translation held until you seal it.
needs: a local model server; licence varies by model

name: trello
line: A Trello board's JSON export: cards, checklists and comments, by list.

name: trips
line: Your trips from booking emails and tickets: where you went, when, and where you stayed.

name: tui
line: A full-screen terminal view to ask, read passages and approve, in curses.

name: typos
line: Forgives misspellings in questions.

name: typosquat
line: Dependency names a letter off from a popular one (reqeusts, lodahs), checked against a list of top packages you downloaded.

name: upgrade-notes
line: Before an upgrade: the changelog lines between the version you lock and the one you'd move to, from the package's own files.
network: the registry (PyPI, npm or crates.io), to fetch the newer version's changelog

name: upstream-desk
line: Your work in other people's projects, in one place: notifications sorted into what needs you, and your open pull requests there.
network: GitHub, through gh, with your own login

name: vocab
line: The words you're learning, from your notes and the texts you read, with where you met each one.

name: voice
line: Dictation, calls and lectures transcribed into dated text.

name: wallabag
line: wallabag's JSON or HTML export: saved entries as plain text, with their tags.

name: warm
line: The kernel kept running between questions on this machine, so each question skips the start-up.

name: warranties
line: Receipts and warranties: when the dishwasher's cover ends, and where its receipt is.

name: watch
line: A file re-read the moment it changes (inotify, FSEvents, or polling), so the index is always current.

name: wayback
line: Each web snapshot paired with the Wayback Machine's nearest copy, so anyone can see what the page said that day.
network: archive.org, to find the nearest archived copy

name: weather-bet
line: Wager on rain tomorrow before you look, against Open-Meteo's own forecast, and see whose Brier score wins.
network: api.open-meteo.com, to read the forecast and the outcome

name: web-pages
line: Saved web pages, .html and .mhtml, as their readable text, with the address they came from.

name: welcome
line: One plain thank-you on a first-time contributor's first pull request, once per person, and only where it's turned on.
network: the forge, through the workflow's token, to post the thank-you

name: why-not
line: When the answer is 'not enough to say', which words found nothing, and what kind of file would have answered.

name: witness
line: A second person's seal beside yours, for answers that need two people to agree.

name: words-ar
line: Arabic common words, with the article and prefixes read apart.

name: words-cy
line: Welsh common words ('a', 'y', 'yn').

name: words-hi
line: Hindi common words ('और', 'है').

name: words-ja
line: Japanese, which has no spaces: a small segmenter of its own and a common-words list.

name: words-pl
line: Polish common words ('i', 'w').

name: words-ru
line: Russian common words, so questions aren't matched on 'и' and 'в'.

name: words-sv
line: Swedish common words ('och', 'att').

name: words-tr
line: Turkish common words ('ve', 'bir').

name: words-zh
line: Chinese, which has no spaces: words found by a small segmenter of its own, and a common-words list.

name: writefreely
line: WriteFreely posts, from its export or a copy of its SQLite database, as dated text.

name: x-archive
line: An X (Twitter) archive: your posts, replies and DMs as dated lines.

name: zotero
line: Your Zotero library, from a copy of zotero.sqlite: items, notes and PDF annotations, each with its citation.
